[[Serbia]] first participated at the [[Olympic Games]] in [[1912 Summer Olympics|1912]] as the [[Kingdom of Serbia]]. The country returned to the Olympics as an independent team after ninety-six years at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]].

== History ==
{{See also|Serbia at the 1912 Summer Olympics}}
Despite not participating at the first Olympic Games in [[1896 Summer Olympics|1896]] in [[Athens]], Serbian King [[Alexander I of Serbia|Aleksandar Obrenović]] attended the Games at the invitation of Greek King [[George I of Greece|George I]]. At these Games [[Momčilo Tapavica]] (born in today's Serbian province [[Vojvodina]]), who competed for [[Kingdom of Hungary]], became the first athlete from today's territory of Serbia and the first ethnic [[Serbs|Serb]] to win an Olympic medal, bronze in tennis.<ref>[http://www.oks.org.rs/takmicenja/olimpijske-igre/letnje-olimpijske-igre/i-igre-atina-1896/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311000851/http://www.oks.org.rs/takmicenja/olimpijske-igre/letnje-olimpijske-igre/i-igre-atina-1896/ |date=2018-03-11 }} Official site of Olympic Committee of Serbia, 1896 Olympic Games (Serbian)</ref> 

The ''Serbian Olympic Club'' was established on February 23, 1910. Major [[Svetomir Đukić]] is considered the founder of the Olympic movement in Serbia. In 1912, the Club changed its name to the [[Olympic Committee of Serbia]] and that year it was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]].<ref>[http://www.oks.org.rs/olimpijski-komitet-srbije/istorija/ History of Olympic Committee of Serbia on official site (Serbian)]</ref>

From the [[1920 Summer Olympics]] to the [[1992 Winter Olympics]], Serbian athletes participated as part of the [[Yugoslavia at the Olympics|Yugoslavia]]n team. At the [[1992 Summer Olympics]], they participated as [[Independent Olympic Participants]] as their nation was under [[United Nations]] sanctions. The continuing sanctions meant that no Serbian athletes competed at the [[1994 Winter Olympics]]. Sanctions were mostly lifted in 1995. From the [[1996 Summer Olympics]] to the [[2006 Winter Olympics]], Serbian athletes participated as part of the [[Serbia and Montenegro at the Olympics|Serbia and Montenegro]] team.

Seven-time Olympian shooter and 1988 gold medalist [[Jasna Šekarić]] competed under four different banners during her twenty-four-year Olympic career. She started under the flag of [[Yugoslavia at the Olympics|Yugoslavia]] in 1988, then she competed as an [[Independent Olympic Participants|Independent Participant]] in 1992, under the flag of [[Serbia and Montenegro at the Olympics|Serbia and Montenegro]] from 1996 to 2004, and in 2008 and 2012 she represented Serbia.

Serbian former basketball player and administrator [[Borislav Stanković]] was the [[Secretary General of FIBA]] from 1976 to 2002, and a member of the [[International Olympic Committee]]. As Secretary General, he pushed for a change in FIBA's rules to allow players from the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) to compete at the Olympics. Prior to the [[1992 Summer Olympics]] in [[Barcelona]], only professionals in leagues other than the NBA were allowed to compete.<ref>{{cite book |last1=McCallum |first1=Jack |title=Dream Team How Michael, Magic, Larry, Charles, and the Greatest Team of All Time Conquered the World and Changed the Game of Basketball Forever |date=2013 |publisher=Random House |isbn=9780345520494 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-8KJGlUvrPYC |access-date=14 May 2020}}</ref>

==Predecessor countries==
The [[Olympic Committee of Serbia]], created in 1910 and recognized in 1912, is deemed the direct successor to both the [[Yugoslav Olympic Committee]] and the Olympic Committee of [[Serbia and Montenegro]] by the [[International Olympic Committee|IOC]].<ref>[http://www.oks.org.rs/olimpijski-komitet-srbije/istorija/?lang=sr-latn] Official site of Olympic Committee of Serbia, History of Olympic Committee (Serbian)</ref> In the period from 1920 to 2006, athletes representing these defunct countries won a total of 99 medals: 95 at the Summer Games and 4 at the Winter Games.
